messages:
Rina Kapoor: Quick design review: in the virtualized compare table the perf badge hover card sometimes jumps when rows recycle during scroll. Repro: open catalog, compare 30+ models, scroll quickly, hover a perf badge mid-scroll. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.test/virt-jump.png :confused:
Evan Morris: yep i hit this too. seems tied to virtualization re-rendering the row node that hosts the tooltip
Diego Alvarez: implementation detail: we mount tooltips on the row DOM by default. with virtualization the DOM node is recycled so the tooltip loses its anchor and repositions -> jump
Priya Shah: proposed UX options: (1) detach tooltip to a fixed overlay (global portal) and anchor by coords, (2) debounce virtualization while a tooltip is open, (3) make perf detail available in a persistent side panel when compare mode > 5 items
accessibility-bot: Accessibility note: option 1 is preferable for focus management. Ensure the tooltip has role="dialog" when it contains interactive content and that focus is trapped if it opens an actionable micropanel. For simple read-only perf info, provide aria-describedby on the badge and avoid focus trap
Rina Kapoor: I prefer 1 + small debounce (100ms) to avoid blocking virtualization perf. Also want to tweak copy: the hover card currently says "Perf: 87" which is ambiguous. Suggest "Perf (latency · cost): 87" and include a 2-line breakdown: latency median, cost/unit
Evan Morris: agree on copy. Also when compact density is on, the hover area is tiny and users accidentally trigger badge hovers when trying to open the compare row menu. We should increase badge hit area (transparent padding) without changing visual density
Diego Alvarez: easy CSS fix: .perf-badge { padding: 6px; margin: -6px; } keeps layout but increases target. For the portal change, here's a quick snippet I tried:
```
// mount tooltip to global overlay and position by anchorRect
const mountTooltipGlobal = (anchorRect, content) => {
  const node = document.getElementById('global-tooltip-layer');
  // position absolute using anchorRect + window scroll
}
```
worked in sandbox, prevented jumps during scroll
Priya Shah: pinning UX: when a row is pinned in compact mode the pin icon gets hidden in virtualization because the pinned state isn't persisted in DOM attributes during recycle. We need a DOM-agnostic indicator (eg small left outline + aria-pressed attribute on the row element)
accessibility-bot: For pinned state, ensure aria-pressed="true" on the pin control and add aria-roledescription="pinned row" to the row container. Also ensure the left outline color meets 3:1 contrast; fallback to a 3px outline if not
Rina Kapoor: design decision: show a 3px left accent in compact mode; on hover show the full pin icon and tooltip "Pinned to version X". Keep stripe color from token: --color-accent-pin. Add a tooltip for keyboard users that appears on focus
Evan Morris: will add keyboard focus visible styles and update the virtualization keying so pinned rows keep stable keys (use model-id instead of index)
Diego Alvarez: note for testing: add unit test that simulates virtualization recycle and asserts that pinned rows keep aria attributes and that tooltip mounting uses global overlay
Priya Shah: I'll update the copy in design tokens and the spec doc: include microcopy for perf card and pinned states. Also add a small accessibility checklist for the PR: contrast, aria-pressed, role/roledescription, focus order
Rina Kapoor: thanks all. action items: Evan -> change tooltip mount to global portal + global debounce 100ms; Diego -> add increased hit area CSS and ensure portal z-index > other controls; Evan/Diego -> make pinned indicator DOM-agnostic and add aria attrs; Priya -> copy + a11y checklist in the PR. tagging @eng-frontend for review :rocket:
Evan Morris: I'll open a draft PR today with screenshots, keyboard tests, and a changelog entry
Diego Alvarez: will add the CSS patch and a small E2E that scrolls while hovering
accessibility-bot: Reminder: include keyboard-only screenshots in PR and run axe-core on storybook stories
Rina Kapoor: perfect. moving this to a Figma review and will ping the thread after the PR lands
